target_customer: Consumers wanting private, temporary social spaces for friends and events (free, no stated payer)
problem: Facebook mixed every relationship into one feed; people wanted small private spaces to share photos, events and talk.
business_model: Free consumer social product, no revenue model stated

founders.name: Austin Chang
founders.background_notes: YC profile lists later product and operating roles.

founders.name: Alex Chung
founders.background_notes: Spelled Alex Chun in one secondary source; YC page says Chung.

competitors.name: Facebook Groups
competitors.what: Group sharing feature relaunched in October 2010 that resembled The Fridge
competitors.traction_then: Facebook had hundreds of millions of users

competitors.name: Yahoo Groups and Ning
competitors.what: Existing group sharing hubs named in TechCrunch launch coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: A social web app with groups and media upload; standard engineering for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Features copyable by Facebook and others; a network only forms inside each small group.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook launched Groups in October 2010 as a similar feature; Google acquired the team in July 2011 for Google+ and the service shut for users.

market_need_then: Privacy complaints about Facebook were common in 2010; growth was 30,000 registered users and 20,000 groups by early 2011 per The Next Web.

branding.domain_note: Used frid.ge, a domain hack; the .com not used. frid.ge returned 503 when fetched.

brand_strength.rationale: A fridge metaphor and memorable domain hack, but no sources on community or brand press, and the name is a very generic word.

outcome_analysis: The Fridge made private disposable group networks and reached tens of thousands of users, but Facebook launched a similar Groups feature in late 2010. Google bought the team in July 2011 for Google+ at an undisclosed price and the product was shut down for existing users, a soft landing instead of a lasting product.
notes: Press totals conflict: one outlet says 800K raised and CB Insights lists 200K total; neither matches the 80K in aggregators. No page with a verifiable round date and source was opened, so no round is recorded. Google announced the acquisition in July 2011 with terms undisclosed.
